---
title: What sync rewrites, and what it leaves alone
version: 1
---

**Lesson 2 said the native projects are yours to edit, and that is true of almost every file in
them.** A few are Capacitor's, rewritten on every `cap sync` or `cap update`, and an edit to one of
those disappears without a word. They say so in their first lines:

```
ana@dev:~/planner$ head -n 4 ios/App/CapApp-SPM/Package.swift
// swift-tools-version: 5.9
import PackageDescription

// DO NOT MODIFY THIS FILE - managed by Capacitor CLI commands
ana@dev:~/planner$ head -n 1 android/app/capacitor.build.gradle
// DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE! IT IS GENERATED EACH TIME "capacitor update" IS RUN
```

The rule is easy to test. Change the app's name in `strings.xml`, which belongs to you, and add a
line to `capacitor.build.gradle`, which belongs to Capacitor. Then sync:

```
ana@dev:~/planner$ sed -i 's/>Study planner</>Planner</' android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
ana@dev:~/planner$ sed -i '1a // a line of mine' android/app/capacitor.build.gradle
ana@dev:~/planner$ git status --short
 M android/app/capacitor.build.gradle
 M android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
ana@dev:~/planner$ npx cap sync android
✔ Copying web assets from dist to android/app/src/main/assets/public in 8.14ms
✔ Creating capacitor.config.json in android/app/src/main/assets in 944.33μs
✔ copy android in 17.57ms
✔ Updating Android plugins in 1.12ms
✔ update android in 19.50ms
[info] Sync finished in 0.044s
ana@dev:~/planner$ git status --short
 M android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
ana@dev:~/planner$ grep app_name android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
    <string name="app_name">Planner</string>
```

**Before the sync both files were changed; after it, one was.** `capacitor.build.gradle` was written
again from what Capacitor knows, and the line was gone, with nothing in the output to say so. The name
in `strings.xml` stayed, because sync never touches it. Here both edits were put back afterwards with
`git checkout android`.

| written by sync or update, every time | yours, never touched |
|---|---|
| `android/app/src/main/assets/public/` and the two JSON files beside it | `AndroidManifest.xml`, `strings.xml`, `styles.xml` |
| `android/app/capacitor.build.gradle`, `android/capacitor.settings.gradle` | `android/app/build.gradle`, `variables.gradle` |
| `android/capacitor-cordova-android-plugins/` | `MainActivity.java` and any Java or Kotlin you add |
| `ios/App/App/public/`, `capacitor.config.json`, `config.xml` | `Info.plist`, `AppDelegate.swift`, `SceneDelegate.swift` |
| `ios/App/CapApp-SPM/Package.swift` | the Xcode project's build settings, icons and signing |

**A setting you want in a Capacitor file goes in `capacitor.config.ts` instead**, where Capacitor
reads it and writes it out again every time. And git is what makes the rule safe to learn: `git status`
after a sync shows anything Capacitor changed, and `git diff` shows what.
